trial_court: Principal Senior Civil Judge, Eluru, OP No.38 of 2000
case_name: Grandham Sridhar vs Smt. Grandham Jaya Vani
facts_of_case: The marriage was performed on 10.04.1996. The husband filed for dissolution of marriage. The trial court dismissed the petition and allowed the wife's counter claim for restitution of conjugal rights.

legal_principles.principle: The burden is on the party to prove cruel acts.
legal_principles.held: The burden is on the appellant to prove the cruel acts on the part of the respondent.

legal_principles.principle: Mental cruelty can be caused by refusal to have sexual intercourse, making defamatory allegations, and filing repeated false complaints.
legal_principles.held: It was held in Vidhya Viswanathan v Kartik Balakrishnan that refusal to have sexual intercourse for considerable period by wife amounts to mental cruelty. It was also held in K.Srinivas Rao v D.A.Deepa that making undoubted, indecent defamatory allegations against the spouse or his or her relatives in the pleadings, filing of complaints or issuing notices or news items which may have adverse impact on the business prospects or the job of the spouse and filing repeated false complaints would, in the facts of a case amount to causing mental cruelty.

outcome.final_order: The appeal was allowed, and the order dated 03/12/2004 was set aside.

use_for_drafting: representing clients in family court proceedings
